title: Proteomic profiling of the parasitic nematode Ascaridia galli
projectDescription: Ascaridia galli (A. galli) is one of the most common intestinal nematodes of domesticated chickens and the cause of avian ascaridiasis, a globally important disease in poultry.  Its genome is sparsely sequenced and its proteome is uncharacterized. We her investigate the proteome composition in larvae and in female and male worms of A. Galli, querying the LC-MS/MS data against a hybrid database of two related nematodes; Ascaris suum and Anisakis simplex. We compare the proteome of larvae, female and male worms.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The intestinal hen nematode Ascaridia galli (A. galli) were prepared to isolate larvae, female worms and male worms. Worms and larvae were mashed and the protein samples were digested into peptides using the S-Trap-based digestion according to the manufacturer's protocol for micro spin columns (Protifi, USA). Briefly, the protein pellet was solubilized in 5% SDS, and proteins are further denatured by acidification to pH < 1 by phosphoric acid, and cysteine residues were reduced by TCEP and blocked by MMTS, respectively. Trypsin was added to the protein pellet (2 µg to male and female, and 1 µg to larvae) in 50 mM TEAB pH 8. Trypsin cleavage was performed for two hours at 47oC. After elution from the S-trap column the peptide samples were vacuum-dried and resolubilized in 2% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid, prior to LC-MS/MS analyses. The peptide samples were analyzed by nano liquid chromatography (Easy-nLC 1200, Thermo Scientific)-tandem mass spectrometry (Q-Exactive HF-X Hybrid Quadrupole Orbitrap, Thermo Scientific), essentially as previously described. Peptides were trapped on a pre-column (Acclaim PepMap 100 C18, pore size: 100 Å, particle diameter: 3 µm, inner diameter: 75 µm, length: 2 cm, Thermo Scientific) and separated on a reverse phase analytical column (PepMap RSLC C18, pore size: 100 Å, particle diameter: 2 µm, inner diameter 75 µm, length 25 cm, Thermo Scientific) using a 60 mins gradient from 5-90% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid at a 270 nL/min flowrate. The MS was operated in positive mode and higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with collision energy (NCE) of 30 was applied for peptide fragmentation. Full scan (MS1) resolution was 60,000 and Automatic Gain Control (AGC) target set at 3×106 with scan range between 392-1,700 m/z. Data-dependent analysis (DDA) was applied to fragment up to 12 of the most intense peaks in MS1. Resolution for fragment scans (MS2) was set at 15,000. Dynamic exclusion was set at 15 seconds and unassigned and +1 charge states were excluded.
dataProcessingProtocol: Thermo Proteome Discoverer 3.0 (Thermo Scientific), was used to identify and quantify the protein origin of the peptides in the samples, by default label-free quantification workflow including INFERYS Rescoring. The query was tailored to include multiple Clade III nematode proteomes because the proteome for A. galli exists only for mitochondrial DNA. Ascaris suum (10,484 sequences, from Uniprot 06/23/2025) and Anisakis simplex (25,719 sequences, from Uniprot 09/28/2025) were selected as suitable comparison proteomes along with the 91 A. galli sequences (Uniprot 09/28/2025). The sample names indicate replicate number (a-c) and larva=larvae, fem=female and male.
